summary: LunaSight is an interactive lunar exploration and preliminary landing-site planning platform designed to help mission planners, researchers, students, and educators understand the challenges of landing near the Moon’s South Pole. Using a 3D Moon visualization, users can explore landing locations, examine lunar terrain, and observe how sunlight, Earth visibility, and communication conditions change over time. By combining NASA lunar data, lunar orientation models, live NOAA space-weather information, and simulated communication relays, LunaSight makes complex lunar mission conditions easier to visualize and compare.
details:
LunaSight addresses the challenges of selecting safe and suitable lunar landing locations, particularly near the Moon’s South Pole, where sunlight and direct communication with Earth can be blocked by mountains and crater rims. Through an interactive 3D Moon, users can explore landing locations, examine terrain and elevation, track Sun and Earth positions, monitor live space-weather conditions from NOAA, and visualize simulated communication relay networks. It combines NASA lunar imagery and elevation resources with lunar orientation models to make complex mission conditions easier to understand for planners, researchers, and educators.

Our next step is to develop more accurate terrain-aware horizon calculations, predict sunlight and communication windows, enable side-by-side comparisons of landing sites and dates, and integrate higher-precision NASA SPICE and DONKI data. Our long-term vision is to make LunaSight an accessible decision-support platform for preliminary lunar mission planning and education.
